label: Gerard 40
title: Three-monthly HbA1c monitoring during non-insulin diabetes treatment
statement: It is necessary to monitor the HbA1c level of a patient on antidiabetic drug (other than insulin) every 3 months.

plain_summary: Review HbA1c monitoring during ongoing non-insulin treatment for type 2 diabetes when the last test is over three calendar months old or a full three months without testing is confirmed.

medicine_groups.name: metformin
medicine_groups.note: Count a listed ingredient alone or in a combination used for type 2 diabetes. Count one combination supply once.

medicine_groups.name: DPP-4 inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Count a listed ingredient alone or in a combination used for type 2 diabetes. Count one combination supply once.

medicine_groups.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Count a listed ingredient alone or in a combination used for type 2 diabetes. Count one combination supply once.

medicine_groups.name: Dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonists

needs_facts.meets: Enter the measured HbA1c as a number in % or mmol/mol and use the date of the blood test. Any value documents a test on that date. The interval is overdue only if the most recent test was more than 3 months before the latest date in the record and the other requirements are met.

needs_facts.what: Timing of the most recent HbA1c blood test
needs_facts.meets: Use this answer when the pharmacist can confirm test timing without a numeric result. Count 3 months before the latest date in the record. A test exactly on the cut-off is within the interval. Unknown timing leaves the finding possible.

options.words: The last HbA1c was before the three-month cut-off
No HbA1c was done in the full three months under review. The last date is unknown or the test was never done.
An HbA1c was done on or after the cut-off, within the three months under review

needs_facts.what: Reason for the non-insulin medicine under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only when the reason for this medicine is unclear and would change the finding. Name the medicine in the finding. Count it if it is used for type 2 diabetes, even if it has another use. If it is used only for another condition, assess any other qualifying diabetes medicine separately. An unknown reason stays open.

options.words: Used for type 2 diabetes, alone or with another reason

needs_facts.what: Use of non-insulin diabetes treatment throughout the 3 months before the latest date in the record
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if supply dates, quantities, directions and documented treatment dates leave actual use uncertain. Count documented switches between qualifying medicines. Taken throughout the interval confirms continuity. A confirmed break rules it out. Unknown use leaves continuity open. This answer does not establish test timing.

options.words: Treatment did not cover the full interval

rule_for_models: Use the cut-off 3 months before the latest date in the record. Flag an overdue interval when the record covers the full interval, listed non-insulin treatment for type 2 diabetes continued throughout it, and the most recent HbA1c was before the cut-off or the record confirms that no HbA1c was done during the interval. A test on the cut-off or later in the interval gives no finding. Give no finding if type 2 diabetes is ruled out or qualifying treatment did not cover the interval. Use the individual testing plan as context. Use directions and other recorded indications to decide which medicines count. A medicine used for type 2 diabetes counts even if it also has another use. If a medicine was used only for another condition, check the other listed medicines. Check supply dates, quantities, directions, switches between qualifying medicines and recorded use for continuity. If the evidence is incomplete and the finding is still possible, report only a possible finding. Name "Type 2 diabetes" if the diagnosis is missing. If record coverage is unclear, state the period the record does not show. A dated "HbA1c" result or confirmed test timing is sufficient. If timing is unknown, name only "Timing of the most recent HbA1c blood test" for that gap and give the latest record date. A missing result, an undated value or an unspecified blood test leaves timing open. An answer about indication or use leaves unknown test timing open. Never use the counter entry date as the test date. Clarify conflicting evidence before confirming the interval is overdue. If the indication still changes the decision and the answer can refer to only one medicine, name that medicine and the missing fact "Reason for the non-insulin medicine under review". If several courses could fit the answer, describe which courses need clarification and leave the finding possible without applying one answer to them all. If treatment throughout the interval remains unclear, name "Use of non-insulin diabetes treatment throughout the 3 months before the latest date in the record". Apply an answer only to the medicine or interval it describes. For each finding cite the diagnosis if recorded, an early qualifying supply or treatment line on or before the cut-off, the latest HbA1c test or timing evidence if known, and the evidence of continuing treatment at the latest record date, where available.
cannot_be_seen: Outside pathology results may be missing. Confirm the diabetes indication when a qualifying supply could be for weight management, heart failure or chronic kidney disease. Saxenda, Wegovy including Wegovy FlexTouch, and Liraglutide Lupin can be used for weight management. Some SGLT2 inhibitors can be used for heart failure or chronic kidney disease. A brand or a diagnosis alone does not establish the reason for this supply.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the date of the last HbA1c and review the appropriate interval for this patient?
